notes: Corrected: the resumptive suffix of `לִפְנֵיהֶם` had been marked unrepresented beside a bare `אֲשֶׁר` → *whom*. Rule 22 forbids that where the one English word carries the resumption as well as the relation, so the relative and the suffix now share one unit on *whom*, headed on the relative, while `לִפְנֵי` keeps its own *over*, exactly as the noun keeps *stones* in that rule's `whose` case.
*all them* stays with `כֹל` as rule 31's supplied completion of the quantifier: *them* stands outside the relative clause as its antecedent, so it cannot be the clause-internal resumption.
The marginal note offering *There is no end, in the mind of all the people...* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
